objective_for_doctor:
Age: 58
Sex: Female
Chief Complaint: I have episodes of suffocation, trouble keeping your tongue in your mouth, and a hard time opening/raising one or both eyelids

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi. I’ve been having episodes where it feels like I can’t breathe or I’m suffocating, and I also have trouble keeping my tongue in my mouth. My jaw is hard to open, my neck muscles spasm and feel sore so I can’t turn my head to one side, and my face and neck keep twitching. I was treated in the hospital recently for nausea and agitation/intoxication, and they gave me medication through an IV or a shot.
That sounds very concerning. **One question first:** when these episodes happen, do you stay fully awake and able to understand what’s going on, or do you become confused/unresponsive?
I stay awake and I can understand what’s happening. I’m not confused or unresponsive during the episodes.
Thanks. **Next question:** during the episodes, do you have **any fever**, or did anyone notice **a rash or swelling of your lips/tongue**?
I don’t have a fever, and I haven’t noticed or been told about any rash or swelling of my lips or tongue.
Okay. **Next question:** do you have **stridor** (a harsh, high-pitched sound when breathing in) or is it more like **wheezing** (a whistling sound when breathing out)?
It feels more like I can’t breathe/suffocate, but I don’t know if it’s stridor or wheezing. I haven’t been told what sound it is.
Understood. **Next question:** do you notice these episodes are triggered by **stress/anxiety**, or do they come on **suddenly without any trigger**?
They don’t feel tied to stress or anxiety. They can come on suddenly, without a clear trigger.

Got it. **Next question:** during an episode, do you have **painful muscle stiffness** (like your jaw locking) and do you feel **unable to control your tongue/jaw movements**, or is it more a sensation of tightness without true movement?
Yes—my jaw gets really hard to open, and I feel like I can’t control my tongue/jaw movements. It’s more than just tightness; it feels like my muscles are locking up or pulling.

Thanks—this is helpful. **Next question:** have you ever had **similar episodes after starting or changing a medication** (especially anti-nausea meds like metoclopramide/compazine, antipsychotics, or antidepressants), or after receiving an IV/shot at the hospital?
I think so. I was recently treated in the hospital for nausea and agitation/intoxication, and they gave me medication by IV or a shot, and since then these episodes have been happening.
Thanks. **Next question:** do you remember the name of the IV/shot medication they gave you (or what it was for—e.g., nausea, agitation, “antipsychotic,” “anti-nausea”)?
I don’t remember the exact name. I know it was for nausea and agitation/intoxication, and they gave it through an IV or a shot.
Okay. **Next question:** during episodes, do you have **any eye deviation** (eyes rolling up/sideways) or **tongue protrusion/abnormal facial movements** that others can see?
Yes—my face and neck muscles twitch/spasm, and I have trouble opening/raising one or both eyelids. I’m not sure about eyes rolling to one side or tongue protruding.

Thanks. **Next question:** have you noticed these episodes improve after you receive a medication like **diphenhydramine (Benadryl)** or **benztropine**, or after you’re given an anti-dystonia treatment?
I haven’t had diphenhydramine or benztropine that I remember, so I can’t say if it improves. I don’t know if they gave me an anti-dystonia treatment specifically.
One last focused question: do you have **any trouble swallowing**, drooling, or a “hot potato” muffled voice during the episodes?
No—during the episodes I mainly feel like I can’t breathe/suffocate, and my jaw/tongue/neck and face muscles lock up or spasm. I don’t have drooling or a hot-potato muffled voice.
[DDX] Acute dystonic reactions, Larygospasm, Bronchospasm / acute asthma exacerbation, Panic attack, Acute COPD exacerbation / infection
